purpose: Levorphanol is used to treat moderate to severe pain that other pain medicines cannot control well enough. Doctors may prescribe it for ongoing pain or pain after surgery or injury. It is a strong medicine usually reserved for situations where other options have not worked.
how_it_works: Levorphanol works by attaching to special pain receptors in your brain and spinal cord, kind of like a key fitting into a lock. When it connects to these receptors, it blocks the pain signals traveling through your nervous system so you feel less pain. Think of it like turning down the volume on your body's pain alarm system.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, lightheadedness, and sweating. You may also feel confused or have a dry mouth. These effects are very common with strong pain medicines like this one.
warnings: This is a very strong opioid medicine that can be habit-forming and lead to dependence or addiction. Never take more than prescribed, and never share it with anyone else. It can cause dangerously slow or stopped breathing, especially if combined with alcohol, sleep aids, or other opioids. Keep it locked away and out of reach of children. Tell your doctor right away if you feel overly sleepy or have trouble breathing. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and set carefully by your doctor based on your pain level and how your body responds. A common starting dose for adults is 2 mg by mouth every 6 to 8 hours as needed. Your doctor may adjust the dose over time to find what works best for you while keeping you safe. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions.
